s: A bank wants to decide which of its COBOL batch and CICS online applications on an IBM z/OS mainframe should be modernized to Java on AWS, and in what order. Documentation is outdated, and only a few engineers understand the code. The team needs automated codebase analysis, generated technical documentation, decomposition of the applications into business domains, and a proposed modernization wave plan. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST effort?
o: Use AWS Transform for mainframe to analyze the code, generate documentation, decompose the applications into business domains, plan modernization waves, and refactor selected domains to Java.
Use the AWS Mainframe Modernization managed runtime environment to replatform all applications first, and analyze them after the migration.
Rehost the mainframe workloads on Amazon EC2 by using AWS Application Migration Service.
Hire contractors to document the code manually, and use AWS Migration Hub strategy recommendations to prioritize the applications.

w.y: AWS Transform for mainframe uses AI agents to analyze COBOL code, generate documentation, decompose applications into domains, plan modernization waves and refactor selected domains to Java. It covers every requirement in one managed service, giving the LEAST effort.

o.A: Correct: end-to-end AI-assisted mainframe assessment and modernization.
o.B: The managed runtime is closed to new customers, and it does not provide the required analysis or decomposition.
o.C: Application Migration Service cannot replicate z/OS workloads and does not analyze code.
o.D: Manual documentation is slow, and Migration Hub is closed to new customers.
